correctness.rationale: The order-statistic transformation \((U_{(1)},\ldots,U_{(n)})\mapsto(u,r,z_2,\ldots,z_{n-1})\) has Jacobian \(r^{n-2}\) and factors the joint density into an endpoint/range term and a normalized-shape term. Hence the normalized interior configuration is independent of the endpoints, and translation/scale invariance makes \(Q=S^2/R^2\) a function of shape alone. Conditioning on endpoints reduces the interior points to iid uniform points on \([0,1]\), from which the stated mean follows by elementary second moments. Combining independence with the standard beta moments of the uniform range gives the covariance formula. The exact-rational verifier was inspected and an independent symbolic reduction reproduced the closed covariance expression and the \(q=1\) simplification.

originality.rationale: The central structural step is a standard uniform-order-statistics fact: conditional on the sample minimum and maximum, the remaining observations are distributed as an iid uniform sample on the random interval, equivalently the normalized spacings are independent of location and range. Since sample variance is translation invariant and homogeneous of degree two, independence of \(S^2/R^2\) from the endpoints follows immediately. The mean and covariance family then require only elementary moments and the standard beta law for the uniform range, which the recent range literature also records. Under implication-level originality, the full claim is therefore a routine consequence of textbook order-statistic structure rather than a new statistical theorem.
